title: Aliens
build: US Activision disk, 'Aliens [Activision].d64', a cracked copy: a Remember cracktro and trainer (22 KB BASIC file at $0801) in front of ten packed game files A0-A9

records.c: The level's sprites, 64 bytes to a frame: $00 the squad's marines (drawn by marines_draw), $01 its shadow, the alien $02 and its smaller appearing and fading frames $03-$05, then the blast $06-$0D.
Sprite frames $04-$07.
Sprite frames $08-$0B.
Sprite frames $0C-$0F.
The maze's multicolour character set: the ducts' walls and corners, the grid labels and the signs.
Characters $40-$7F.
The level's entry points: start ($8000) and restart ($8002), both level_init. The object table addresses after them are all $8028 too: the level uses no engine objects.
Object table 1, low byte.
Object table 1, high byte.
Object table 2, low byte.
Object table 2, high byte.
Object table 3, low byte.
Object table 3, high byte.
Object table 4, low byte.
Object table 4, high byte.
Object table 5, low byte.
Object table 5, high byte.
Object table 6, low byte.
Object table 6, high byte.
Object table 7, low byte.
Object table 7, high byte.
Object table 8, low byte.
Object table 8, high byte.
Object table 9, low byte.
Object table 9, high byte.
Object table 10, low byte.
Object table 10, high byte.
Object table 11, low byte.
Object table 11, high byte.
Object table 12, low byte.
Object table 12, high byte.
Object table 13, low byte.
Object table 13, high byte.
Object table 14, low byte.
Object table 14, high byte.
Object table 15, low byte.
Object table 15, high byte.
Object table 16, low byte.
Object table 16, high byte.
Object table 17, low byte.
Object table 17, high byte.
Object table 18, low byte.
Object table 18, high byte.

Starts the level: resets the stack, sets the text origin, selects VIC-II bank 1, points the raster call at raster_frame ($905D), clears the end flag $06B9, sets the end delay $06BA to 60 passes and sets the VIC-II from the list after the call.
The last pairs of the VIC-II list: sprite colours ($D02B-$D02E); $FF would end it.

Latches the collisions, waits a frame, sets the grace count $06AA (15 passes before aliens come), clears the objects ($80-$FF) and the workspace ($0608-$0688), points the squad's sprite drawing at frame $00 ($4000), starts the squad above the maze (y $EA), draws its marines (marines_draw), sets the sprite pointers from start_frames, turns off the engine's sprite placing ($045A), colours and draws the screen (screen_build) and turns it on.

Once every two frames: the alien catching the squad (catch_check), the squad (squad_move), the aliens (aliens_move), the camera and sprites (camera_sprites), then after the first frame the scroll (scroll_screen). With sprites behind ducts it restores their saved order. Ends when $06B9 is set, or when no marines are left ($0204 and $0203 both 0), after $06BA more passes: stage_complete.
A JMP $8028 (level_init) after the jump to stage_complete, which nothing reaches. Named by the trainer of level 6, which writes a JMP $814F here when that level is loaded.
The low byte of that unreached JMP's address; also the second byte of the level 6 trainer's JMP.
The high byte of that unreached JMP's address; also the third byte of the level 6 trainer's JMP.
The eight sprites' starting frames: the aliens frame $02, the squad frame $00 (its marines) and its shadow frame $01.

The squad: nothing once the level has ended. While an alien holds it ($0670), only a fresh press of fire does anything: a grenade, which costs a marine (marine_lose), blows up the holding alien ($06A1, state 5 for 8 passes) and roars (sfx_roar). Otherwise it walks.
start_effect's argument: $3463 (sfx_roar).
The JMP past the walking code while an alien holds the squad. The level 4 trainer writes $AD here (LDA), so the squad walks on while held.
The grace count $06AA runs down, except while the squad still stands at the start with it at $3F.
The squad wins when it reaches x $0740, y $BE: the duct out at the bottom of column 29 ($06B9 = 1).

Keeps the marine sprites on ($06B8 into bits 6 and 7 of $AC), then finds the directions open where the squad stands (dirs_here): at a junction the map's, between junctions left and right ($0A) or up and down ($05), into $0616.
The joystick's direction (joy_dirs), or down while the squad is still above the maze (y $A9 or more).
A direction that is open becomes the way it walks ($AA), only one of them and a new one first.
A direction that is not open here: if the squad is close to a junction, just ahead or just behind, where that way is open, it walks to it to turn there; otherwise it stops.
Walks one step the way of the lowest bit in $AA (squad_steps), then lets duct_step stop it at the first junction closed that way.
Copies the squad's place to its shadow sprite (object 7) and its open directions to $0617.
Part of the shadow copy: the y.
The camera $A0/$A1 follows the squad (half its x less $A0, held between 0 and $2D6); the fine scroll; then each object's sprite x and y, its x high bit ($0474) and whether it shows ($0479).
The fine scroll for this pass, with any shake ($066F), and its sprite offset $C1.
For each object from 7 down, if on in $AC: its screen x (half its x less the camera, plus $2A), y (plus $3C); off if out of the window.
Named by the trainer of level 1 (its first byte), which lies here when that level is loaded; in this level it stores the sprite x high byte.
Named by the trainer of level 1 (the second byte of its JMP).
Named by the trainer of level 1 (the third byte of its JMP); in this level it adds the window's top to the sprite y.

Then whether the object is in a crossing of ducts: in a cell of type 2 a sprite moving up or down goes behind the characters, in type 8 one moving left or right ($047F, sprite priority); an exploding alien never does.
When the camera has moved to a new column, notes which way ($AB, +1 or -1) and builds that column (column_build). Then the fine scroll into the $D016 copy $047A.

With any sprite behind the ducts, saves the sprite positions and pointers ($0671, $0600) and deals them out again so the sprites flagged in $068C take the low numbers, with their colours, priority, enable and multicolour bits.
Then the sprites not flagged.

When the camera has moved a column, waits for raster line $3C and moves the 25 rows of the screen at $5C00 one character left or right, then writes the new column from $0638 at the edge it came in from.
Scrolling left: each row's 39 characters move one to the left (the copy addresses in the code at $8638 and $863B).
The low byte of the left scroll's source address, written by scroll_screen (one character right of the destination).
The high byte of the left scroll's source address.
The low byte of the left scroll's destination address.
The high byte of the left scroll's destination; then the next row, 40 bytes on.
Scrolling right: each row's characters move one to the right (the copy addresses in the code at $8682 and $8685).
The low byte of the right scroll's source address.
The high byte of the right scroll's source address.
The low byte of the right scroll's destination address (one character right of the source).
The high byte of the right scroll's destination; then the next row, 40 bytes on.
The new column, 25 characters, into column 0 or column 39.

Builds one screen column into $0638: for each of the eight rows of cells, the three characters of the cell's tile at that column (tile_of, tile_char), then the bottom row: the exit's marker under column 29, or blank; past the maze's end, 25 blanks.
The tile of map cell X: the map byte ($9430), or its low five bits less 2 when bit 5 is set, as an index into tile_lo/tile_hi; the tile's address into $C1/$C2.

A tile's character, except that a blank in the top row of a cell, in rows 1 to 6 and odd columns, becomes the cell's grid label: a letter by column (label_letters) in its second character, a number by row (label_digits) in its third, and character $60 in its fourth.
Named by the trainer of level 5, which pokes here when that level is loaded; in this level the operand of tile_char's LDA $BC.
The grid labels' numbers, by row of cells.
The grid labels' letters, one for each two columns of cells.
The joystick's four bits (up, down, left, right) as the maze's direction bits (up 4, down 1, left 2, right 8).
The squad's step for each direction, four bytes (x low, x high, y low, y high): right +3, up -1, left -3, down +1.
The x high bytes of the same steps.
The y low bytes.
The y high bytes.
The characters under the exit at the bottom of column 29.

Colours the screen ($08 for the maze, $09 for the first and last three rows, $0F for each third row) and draws the 40 columns the camera starts on: eight rows of ten cells, each cell's tile four characters by three; the bottom row blank.
Named by the trainer of level 3, which writes an LDA here when that level is loaded; in this level the branch of the colour fill.
Named by the trainer of level 3, which writes an LDA here when that level is loaded; in this level the offset of the branch that closes the loop over the coloured rows.
Named by the trainer of level 6, which writes $AD here; in this level the operand of the STA that steps the screen address.
Named by the trainer of level 6, a second $AD; in this level the cell count's test.
Named by the trainer of level 6, a third $AD; in this level the step to the next row of cells.

The six aliens, from 5 down. An empty one after the grace count: aliens 5 to 2 come out of a vent near the squad (alien_spawn, one a pass); aliens 0 and 1 follow it, appearing every 32 passes where the squad stood 16 passes before, heading its way (alien 1 only near the start, x below $300).
Appearing (state 1): frames $05 down to $02 from alien_appear, one every eight passes; then hunting (state 2) for 64 to 127 counts, one count every four passes.

Hunting: gone when off the screen (alien_onscreen). If it sees the squad (alien_sees) it chases, white, for $60 counts, with sfx_alarm when the chase begins; otherwise it wanders in random colours (wander_colours) and fades (state 3) when its count runs out.
start_effect's argument: $3582 (sfx_alarm).
After the alarm (or straight on if the chase had begun), the mode $0660 = 2, chasing; wandering sets 1. The mode is kept for the alien in $0620.
At a junction it picks a way: towards the squad, on the axis where it is further off, never back the way it came while wandering; with no way open its count is set to 0.
Named by the trainer of level 2, which pokes here when that level is loaded; in this level the alien's junction test.
Not while it holds the squad: it moves, three passes in four while wandering, every pass while chasing with an extra step every 16, then duct_step keeps it to the ducts.
Named by the trainer of level 5, which pokes here when that level is loaded; in this level it stores the alien's new x.
Blown up (state 5): counts down; at 7 the sprite moves to centre the blast; frames $0D-$06 (blast_frames) and the screen shakes (shake_x, shake_y). Fading (state 3): frames $04-$02, then gone.
The aliens' sprites on in $AC, with the marine sprites' bits kept.
An appearing alien's frames, by its count: $05 first, $02 (the whole alien) last.
A fading alien's frames: $02, then $03 and $04.
A blown-up alien's frames.
The sideways shake added to the fine scroll as an alien blows up.
The vertical fine scroll ($D011 copy) during the blast.
For each direction, the opposite one, which a wandering alien does not take.
The colours a wandering alien flickers through.
Moves object X one step the way Y (a direction bit): alien_dx_lo, alien_dx_hi and alien_dy.
An alien's step across, by direction bit: left -3, right +3.
The high bytes of an alien's steps across.
An alien's step down, by direction bit: down +1, up -1.
A routine nothing calls: a sight test like alien_sees, looking along the ducts from object X towards the squad and returning 0 or 1; probably an earlier version.
From object X to the squad: the distance across $BB/$BC and down $BD, and the ways towards it, across in $BF (8 right, 2 left) and down in $C0 (1 down, 4 up).
The map cell under object X (column x/64, row y/24) in X, its type (the map's low four bits; a crossing gives the object's own direction) in A, and the row's top y in $C3.
The open directions of map cell X; a crossing ($02 or $08) counts as open every way ($0F).

Draws the marines left (the bits of $0204) as small figures into sprite frame $00 at $4000, the squad's sprite: rows of three, two, and three. Sets the sprite multicolours by whether any are left; with none ($0203 = 0) the level ends ($06B9) and the marine sprites go off.
The figure patterns, two bytes for each pair of marines.
The second byte of each pair.
The figure's shape, one mask a row.
How many marines each row of figures holds: three, two, and three.

An alien that is hunting and close to the squad (within 6 across and 3 down) and whose sprite is on the same side of the ducts holds it ($0670, alien in $06A1). Each pass it holds, its count $0663 runs down from 90; at 0 a marine is lost (marine_lose).
The count down of the hold. The level 4 trainer writes $BD here (LDA), so the hold never takes a marine.
Takes the highest marine left from $0204 (bit 7 first); with none left $0203 = 0. Redraws the squad (marines_draw). The level 4 trainer writes an RTS here, so grenades and holds cost nothing.
Whether object X can see the squad straight along a duct, with no wall or crossing between: 0 if it can, 1 if not.
Named by the trainer of level 2, which pokes here when that level is loaded; in this level the operand of the sight test's CMP #$04 (looking up).
Named by the trainer of level 5, which pokes here when that level is loaded; in this level the sight test's low byte compare.
Named by the trainer of level 5; in this level the offset of the sight test's branch when the way left is shut.
Not seen: 1.
Seen: 0.
The raster call: unless the main loop is busy ($0463), copies the sprite pointers $06A2 to the screen's $5FF8; then level_frame.
Whether object X is off the screen (y $A9 or more, or x outside the camera's window): then the alien is removed (state 0) and the answer is 1; otherwise 0.

Once a pass: the squad's zone (zone_of) gives two zones for vents (spawn_zone_a, spawn_zone_b), less any zone an alien already came from; up to ten random cells are tried for one in a free zone, and the alien appears there (state 1) heading for the squad.
Named by the trainer of level 5, which pokes here when that level is loaded; in this level the low byte of the STA $0610,X that sets the new alien's direction.
For each zone the squad is in, the first zone aliens come from.
The second.

The zone of the cell under object X, from zones: the low nibble, or the high one when a test of $0610 is set. The test indexes $0610 by half of $BB, which the routine does not set, and ANDs with zero-page $05 rather than #$05.
Named by the trainer of level 5; in this level the operand of zone_of's LDA $BB.

Moves an object from its old place ($B3-$B5) towards its new one ($AF-$B1) a step at a time the way X, stopping at the first junction that is closed that way (or at any junction, when A is not 0); the place reached is left in $AF-$B1.
The directions open at the place $B3-$B5: 0 between junctions, else the cell's (dirs_cell).
The open directions of the map cell at row Y and x $B3/$B4; in a crossing ($02 or $08), only the direction already held ($B7).
Named by the trainer of level 5, which pokes here when that level is loaded; in this level the shift of the cell's column.
duct_step's step across, by direction (down, left, up, right): left -2, right +2.
The high bytes of duct_step's steps across.
duct_step's step down: down +1, up -1.
The direction bit for each of the four.
Y = the row of cells for the y in A (24 lines each); A = the line within it.
The low bytes of each tile's address.
The high bytes.
The tiles, twelve characters each: four across and three down.

The maze, 32 cells across and 8 down, one byte a cell: its tile and, in the low four bits, the directions open from it (1 down, 2 left, 4 up, 8 right); $02 and $08 alone mark a crossing, where one duct passes over another.
For each cell of the maze, two zones of four bits, used to choose where aliens come out.
Bytes after the zones, to $97FF, which no code in the level names.
Data in unpack_inline's packing (its first run goes to $7440), which no code in this level names.
More of the packed data at $E000, $E400-$E7FF.
More of the packed data at $E000, $E800-$EBFF.
More of the packed data at $E000, $EC00-$EFFF.
The rest, to $F2AF; zeros follow.
